_meta.feast: Synaxis of the Three Holy Hierarchs: Basil the Great, Gregory the Theologian, and John Chrysostom
_meta._note: OCA does not publish a Matins DOCX for this feast. Matins from St-Sergius Emenaion (yy/archaic register). Two canons, both by John Mauropus, Metropolitan of Euchaita: Canon I in Tone II (acrostic 'I proclaim the three suns of the light of the threefold Sun'); Canon II in Tone VIII. The Theotokos canon by John Mauropus mentioned in the PDF rubric is omitted (parish practice typically uses only the two hierarchical canons). Magnificat is suppressed at Ode 9; replaced by a custom refrain 'Magnify, O my soul, the three great luminaries among the hierarchs!'. Katavasiae are the irmoi of the Meeting (Feb 2).

troparion.text:
In that ye share in the ways of the apostles,
O teachers of the whole world,
entreat the Master of all,
that He grant peace to the world//
and great mercy to our souls.
troparion.label: Troparion of the holy hierarchs

kontakion.text:
The sacred heralds of divine proclamation,
the foremost among the teachers,
hast Thou received, O Lord,
into the enjoyment of Thy good things and into rest;
for Thou hast accepted their labors and death as surpassing any wholeburnt offering,//
O Thou Who alone dost glorify Thy saints.
kontakion.label: Kontakion of the holy hierarchs

sedalion.text:
Let us all praise Basil as the royal adornment of the Church, the inexhaustible treasury of dogmas;
for he hath instructed us to worship the Holy Trinity Which is united in essence but separate in hypostasis.
sedalion.label: Sessional Hymn (after Kathisma 1)

glory.text:
O divinely wise fathers, most radiant luminaries of the Church of Christ,
ye have enlightened the world with your teachings,
withering the errors of all the heretics, and quenching the flaming tumults of the blasphemous.
Wherefore, as holy hierarchs of Christ, pray ye, that we be saved.

bothNow.text:
O all-hymned Virgin, Mother of Christ God, Mary, Bride of God who knewest not wedlock,
intercession for the faithful, O Sovereign Lady Theotokos:
from every misfortune and all want deliver those who with faith and love flee unto thy protection,
O thou who alone art the Bride of God.
bothNow.label: Theotokion

sedalion.text:
Thou wast a pillar of the Church, and wast shown to be a wealth of piety which cannot be stolen away,
O Gregory the Theologian.
Thou didst illumine thy life with dispassion, and didst make plain the dogmas of the Trinity.
O venerable father, entreat Christ God for the salvation of our souls.
sedalion.label: Sessional Hymn (after Kathisma 2)

glory.text:
Hovering like wise bees over the meadow of the Scriptures,
ye embraced well the most excellent pollen of their flowers,
and together ye have produced for all the faithful the honey of your teachings unto their utter delight.
Wherefore, each of us, delighting therein, crieth out with gladness:
even after death be ye advocates for us who praise you, O blessed ones.

bothNow.text:
Tempest-tossed by the threefold-waves of the passions,
I who lack a conscience fervently call upon thee, O most pure one:
Disdain me not, lest I perish, wretch that I am,
O thou who hast given birth to the Abyss of mercy;
for I have no other hope than thee.
Let me not become a joy unto mine enemies, nor a byword, for I trust in thee.
For whatsoever thou desirest thou canst do, in that thou art the Mother of the God of all.
bothNow.label: Theotokion

magnification.refrain:
We magnify you, O holy hierarchs of Christ—
Basil the Great, Gregory the Theologian and John Chrysostom,
and we honor your holy memory;
for ye entreat Christ God on our behalf.
verses: Hear this, all ye nations; give ear, all ye that inhabit the world.
Glory… Both now… Alleluia… Glory to thee, O God!

sessionalHymns.text:
Let the most wise teachers of the whole world,
who glorified God on earth with their deeds and words,
be magnified today as mediators of salvation for us.
sessionalHymns.label: Sessional Hymn after the Polyeleios

glory.text:
The Church doth celebrate today the honored solemnity of the three teachers;
for they have made the Church steadfast by their divine dogmas.

bothNow.text:
O invincible intercessor for those afflicted, fervent help of those who trust in thee,
deliver me from misfortunes, for thou art the helper of all.
bothNow.label: Theotokion

prokeimenon.refrain:
Thy priests shall be clothed with righteousness,
and Thy righteous shall rejoice.
prokeimenon.verse: My mouth shall speak wisdom, and the meditation of my heart shall be of understanding.

postGospelSticheron.text:
Grace was poured forth in your mouths, O venerable fathers,
and ye became pastors of the Church of Christ,
teaching the reason-endowed sheep to believe in the consubstantial Trinity,
in a single Godhead.
postGospelSticheron.label: Sticheron after Psalm 50

_authors.first: John Mauropus, Metropolitan of Euchaita (Canon I, Tone II; acrostic 'I proclaim the three suns of the light of the threefold Sun')
_authors.second: John Mauropus, Metropolitan of Euchaita (Canon II, Tone VIII)

canon._canonNote: Two hierarchical canons by John Mauropus. The Theotokos canon (also by John Mauropus) mentioned in the Sergius rubric is omitted; parish practice typically uses only the two hierarchical canons. Katavasiae are the irmoi of the Meeting (Feb 2). Magnificat is suppressed at Ode 9; replaced by a custom refrain.

ode1.irmos:
Come, O ye people, let us sing a song to Christ our God,
Who divided the sea, and made a way for the nation
which He had brought up out of the bondage of Egypt;
for He hath been glorified.
ode1.irmos2:
The wonderworking staff of Moses,
striking and dividing the sea in the figure of a cross,
once drowned Pharaoh the pursuing charioteer,
while it saved the fleeing people of Israel as they fled on foot,
chanting a hymn unto God.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
What manner of thanksgiving, what suitable description should we offer to our benefactors,
by whom we have been instructed in a proper life of goodness, O ye people?

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
Most holy Theotokos, save us!
troparia.text:
Theotokion: O all-immaculate one, as with a single mouth, and in singular concord,
we all glorify thee, our common distinction of honor.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
This undertaking is not one that is begun with human zeal; but one aided by wisdom:
seated on Thy throne, O Lover of mankind, grant me the grace of discourse,
that I may be enabled to glorify those whom wisdom itself hath beforehand glorified.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
Like a cup filled to overflowing, O Master,
Thy grace and the great riches of Thy love for mankind have been poured forth
revealing those set forth for praise, to be like angels in the flesh.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
Most holy Theotokos, save us!

ode1.katavasia: The Irmoi of the canon of the feast of the Meeting are sung as katavasiae.

ode3.irmos:
Thou hast established me on the rock of faith,
and my mouth hath been emboldened against mine enemies.
For my spirit rejoiceth when I sing:
There is none as holy as our God
and none more righteous than Thee, O Lord.
ode3.irmos2:
O Christ fortify me on the rock of Thy commandments,
Thou who in the beginning didst establish the heavens with understanding
and didst establish the earth upon the waters,
for there is none holy save Thee, O only Lover of mankind.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
The great trumpet of the Church, the beacon illumining the whole world,
the preacher embracing all the ends of the earth with his proclamations,
Basil of great renown doth inspire this present assembly.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
Radiant beacon of life and actions, radiant beacon of discourse and teachings,
shining more brightly than all, like another sun outshining the stars,
the much hymned Theologian is blessed.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
Lo! the light of the world doth shine upon the world!
Behold, the salt of the earth doth sweeten the earth!
Lo! the tree of life doth bring forth the fruits of immortality, the holy Chrysostom.
All ye who desire to escape death, come ye and take delight!

troparia.refrain: Most holy Theotokos, save us!
troparia.text:
Theotokion: He Who brought all things into being from non-being
and granted being to each creature,
knoweth how to order the given natures as He so desireth.
Hence, who will not marvel on hearing that the Virgin gave birth?

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
The correctors of morals, the edifiers of souls, the common saviors of all,
who have shown us images of godly deeds and discourses,
may the radiant instructors of life be praised with splendor.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
Most holy Theotokos, save us!
troparia.text:
Theotokion: He Who made His abode within the womb of the pure Virgin
hath rendered the souls of the God-bearing saints His dwelling-place,
and through their lips He hath expounded the mystery of His Mother.

sedalenAfterOde3.text:
Together let us praise the great and luminous beacons, the unbreakable pillars of the Church,
delighting in the goodly discourses and the grace of the most wise Chrysostom,
the great Basil and Gregory, the radiant Theologian.
And to them let us cry aloud, giving voice from the depths of our hearts:
O thrice-great holy hierarchs, entreat Christ God,
that He grant forgiveness of sins unto those who celebrate your holy memory with love.
sedalenAfterOde3.label: Sessional Hymn (after Ode 3)

glory.text:
Receiving wisdom from God, like an additional three apostles of Christ,
ye set forth with rational discourse, dogmas,
which beforehand the fishermen through the power of the Spirit set forth in simple words;
for it was fitting that the initial exposition of our Faith be simple.
Wherefore, we all cry out to you: Entreat Christ God,
that He grant remission of sins unto those who celebrate your holy memory with love.
glory.label: Another Sessional Hymn

bothNow.text:
O Theotokos, by the mercy of thy supplications go thou before my humble soul,
engulfed by the waves and storm of life's temptations,
and burdened with the heavy weight of sins,
having become rudderless and nigh to sinking into the depths of Hades,
and grant it peace, rescuing it from misfortunes,
for thou art a calm haven, ever praying to thy Son and God,
that He grant me forgiveness of sins;
for thee do I, thine unworthy servant, have as my hope.
bothNow.label: Theotokion

ode4.irmos:
From a Virgin didst Thou come forth, not as an ambassador, nor as an Angel,
but the very Lord himself incarnate,
and didst save me, the whole man;
wherefore I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!
ode4.irmos2:
Thou, O Lord, art my strength and Thou art my power,
Thou art my God and Thou art my joy,
Thou Who, while never leaving the bosom of Thy Father,
hast visited our poverty.
Therefore with the Prophet Habbakuk I cry unto Thee,
'Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!'

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
O lovers of wisdom, in so far as ye love that which is wise, ye become wise,
teaching all with words;
wherefore marveling at your discourses,
all have thereby been instructed in the disciplines of noetic activity and mystic vision.

troparia.refrain: Most holy Theotokos, save us!
troparia.text:
Theotokion: Like a late morning rain, the Fashioner of the waters and the ages, O all-immaculate one,
descended into thy womb in these later days,
gently cooling those who were fainting.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
A pillar of fire going before the faithful people, consumed the enemies of the Faith
and saved the tribes who followed it,
thus also was the great Basil revealed to be,
such that the Church of Christ might be bold and prevail, enriched by such a champion.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
O Gregory, thy discourse was sweetness to the tongue, the delight of every ear,
the manna of life, a dew of delight, honey from a rock, the heavenly bread of the angels,
moving those who partake thereof to enjoy fully, filling them with sweetness.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
A river of spiritual gifts full to overflowing,
flooding the goodly face of the earth like a torrent of sweetness,
floweth forth from the golden mouth,
delighting and watering every Christian city with the streams of divine waters.

troparia.refrain: Most holy Theotokos, save us!
troparia.text:
Theotokion: O Sovereign Lady, the three God-bearing teachers confessed
that in thy Son the divine nature is simple,
and revealed to be uncommingled with the human nature;
wherefore they proclaimed, that in Him exist two wills and two activities.

ode5.irmos:
O Christ my Savior, the enlightenment of those lying in the darkness of sin.
I rise early to hymn Thee O King of Peace,
enlighten me with Thy radiance,
for I know no other God than Thee.
ode5.irmos2:
O Light never-waning, why hast Thou turned Thy face from me
and why has the alien darkness surrounded me, wretched though I be?
But do Thou guide my steps I implore Thee
and turn me back towards the light of Thy commandments.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
Thou didst permit the saints to drink deeply of the well-spring of Thy gifts,
which in nowise is diminished in flow,
but watereth the whole of creation with the divine torrents flowing from its source,
O Lover of mankind.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
What is gold to me? What are riches and glory and power to me?
They are but smoke dispersed upon the winds!
Let them all vanish; let the wind bear them away!
Mine only cherished riches are the trinity of eloquent teachers.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
The river of immortality poureth forth incorruptible sustenance and divine drink:
providing sustenance for those who hunger, and the beverage of incorruptibility for those who thirst.
Its water is eternally living and sustaineth the life of those who drink of it.
Partake ye all of its ever-flowing life!

troparia.refrain: Most holy Theotokos, save us!
Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
With thankful voices let us praise the wise sages of things human and divine,
who in their love of the Truth revealed unto us the nature of things,
describing their Creator unto all, as is meet.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
With their wise doctrinal discourses and skills the godly healers of men's souls
sweetened that which is bitter and provided an astringent cure for salvation.
O all ye pious, thus adorned, find ye delight and be saved!

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
All discourse falleth silent when the divine preachers utter divine things.
The New Testament hath prevailed over the Old,
having set forth the precious tablets of the new laws therein,
by which the congregation of the faithful are established.

troparia.refrain: Most holy Theotokos, save us!
troparia.text:
Theotokion: The immortal Being passed over mortality to holiness,
and the Virgin Maiden hath surpassed the incorporeal angels,
for she gave birth to God, the King of the angels, upon Whom they are unable to gaze.

ode6.irmos:
The deep abyss of offenses hath surrounded me, O Lord,
but do Thou lead up my life from corruption,
as Thou didst the Prophet Jonah, O Lord.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
Together, O ye three, bless the properties of God:
the unbegottenness of the Father, the begottenness of the Word
and the procession of the Spirit Himself.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
Immeasurably distant from the heights of heaven is the abyss of the earth;
yet divine desire hath borne the saints from the earth higher than the heavens.

troparia.refrain: Most holy Theotokos, save us!
troparia.text:
Theotokion: The three divine preachers,
having thee as a new well-spring and source of mysteries, O Virgin,
adopted a novel mode of speech replete with new sources.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
We have learned to theologize concerning the only Trinity,
and have agreed to hymn the threefold Unity:
having been taught by the fathers to worship the single Essence in three Hypostases.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
The co-beginningless Word and the Spirit of God existed in the beginning with the Father:
the beginningless God is a simple, consubstantial, co-essential Divinity,
as the divine preachers say.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
Most holy Theotokos, save us!
troparia.text:
Theotokion: The Son and the Father, Who was without mother before assuming flesh
and was without father after His incarnation,
these sayings surpass all understanding,
for such most glorious wonders befit God.

kontakion.text:
The sacred heralds of divine proclamation,
the foremost among the teachers,
hast Thou received, O Lord,
into the enjoyment of Thy good things and into rest;
for Thou hast accepted their labors and death as surpassing any wholeburnt offering,//
O Thou Who alone dost glorify Thy saints.
kontakion.label: Kontakion of the hierarchs

ikos.text:
Who can open his lips and move his tongue to breathe forth fire by the power of the Word and the Spirit?
Say but the word, and I will boldly speak;
for these three have transcended human nature in their many and great gifts,
their activity and vision, surpassing both in splendor.
Wherefore, having vouchsafed such great gifts,
in so far as they are Thy faithful servants,
Thou alone hast glorified these Thy saints.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
The former inconstant audacity of heresies is vanquished and doth retreat, O blessed one,
and every debased teaching is shown to be like wax melting in the presence of fire,
struck down by your fiery proclamations.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
They turned away from the false myths of the Greeks
and chose persuasion alone to establish their authority among mankind;
and these three, having established the truth therewith,
triumphed over the whole assembly of the faithful with their discourses, and exhortations.

troparia.refrain: Most holy Theotokos, save us!
troparia.text:
Theotokion: In thee hath every prophecy come to rest and reached its end,
amazing those who say: From thee, O pure one, do the wonders of prophecies pour forth most radiantly,
showing those who utter them to be wise.

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
The divinely eloquent ones were pillars of virtue and wisdom,
whether they kept silent or spake, whether they watched or listened,
commanding us by their words and deeds to cry: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

troparia.refrain: Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
Holy Hierarchs of Christ, pray to God for us!
troparia.text:
Stones shall be launched from the stone-bows of their tongues,
crushing those corrupted by false doctrines,
if any among the blasphemers dare refuse to exclaim: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

troparia.refrain: Most holy Theotokos, save us!
troparia.text:
Theotokion: He Who buildeth with the elements,
and transformeth nature as He so desireth,
made His abode within thee and left thee a virgin even after thou hast given birth,
O Mary, Birthgiver of God.
To Him do we now cry out with thee, O all-immaculate one: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

ode8.irmos:
God Who descended into the fiery furnace with the Hebrew children,
and transformed the flame into dew,
do ye works hymn, and supremely exalt as Lord throughout all ages.

troparia.refrain: We praise, bless, and worship the Lord, singing and exalting Him throughout all ages!
We praise, bless, and worship the Lord, singing and exalting Him throughout all ages!
troparia.text:
The three divine preachers have united themselves, joining together to form a trinity,
and preserving themselves inseparable by their sacred nature;
have thus received a single, indivisible glory,
which doth summon all those who supremely exalt the Trinity throughout the ages,
to a common praise.

troparia.refrain: Most holy Theotokos, save us!
We praise, bless, and worship the Lord, singing and exalting Him throughout all ages!
troparia.text:
Lest he who rendereth praise favors one above the other,
God hath united the three in a unity of equal honor,
esteeming them equal in their gifts, that He might grant them to chant equal hymns, singing:
Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him throughout all ages!

troparia.refrain: We praise, bless, and worship the Lord, singing and exalting Him throughout all ages!
troparia.text:
The mighty and invincible champions of the Godhead, the true allies of the Truth,
having tested well the depths of the Spirit,
setting forth their divine contemplations concerning God,
and teaching us to chant: Ye people, supremely exalt Christ throughout all ages!

troparia.refrain: We praise, bless, and worship the Lord, singing and exalting Him throughout all ages!
troparia.text:
From heaven two magnificent luminaries have enlightened the earth,
one after the other according to their preeminence;
but the three all-great luminaries illumine the whole world more brightly,
chanting together: Ye people, supremely exalt Christ throughout all ages!

troparia.refrain: Most holy Theotokos, save us!
troparia.text:
Theotokion: For our sake God deigned to become incarnate and undergo His honored sufferings,
for our sake He dwelt among mankind;
and though He had not tasted of death and was free from passions,
through a union with mortal flesh He partook of suffering and death.
Wherefore with His Mother, let us supremely exalt Christ throughout all ages!

ode9.irmos:
God the Word, God of God,
Who by ineffable wisdom came to create Adam anew
after his grievous fall to corruption through eating
and Who took flesh beyond all telling from the Holy Virgin for our sake,
Him we faithful with one accord magnify in song.
ode9.irmos2:
Heaven was stricken with awe, and the ends of the earth were filled with amazement,
for God hath appeared in the flesh,
and thy womb was rendered more spacious than the heavens.
Wherefore, the ranks of men and of angels
magnify thee as the Theotokos.
ode9.megalynarion: Magnify, O my soul, the three great luminaries among the hierarchs!
ode9._megalynarionNote: Magnificat is suppressed; this refrain replaces it before the hierarchs' canon troparia (Canon I uses 'three great luminaries among the hierarchs'; Canon II uses 'three pastors of the most holy Trinity', etc.).

troparia.refrain: Magnify, O my soul, the three great luminaries among the hierarchs!
troparia.text:
Lo! your crop, the flock for which ye endured the greatest of pangs,
having assembled and received you three together,
hath your most sweet union as their common boast.

troparia.refrain: Magnify, O my soul, the three luminaries of the Church of Christ!
troparia.text:
Grace wielded not a two-edged sword, but one with three edges against the foe,
a single blade forged in heaven and sharpened with threefold might,
which ever fighteth for the one thrice-radiant Godhead.

troparia.refrain: Magnify, O my soul, those who illumine the Church of Christ!
troparia.text:
Your residence was in the heavens, O most glorious ones,
with those bearing flesh eternally undefiled;
and dwelling most perfectly now among them, entreat those who are most high,
that they take thought and pray for us who abide yet on earth.

troparia.refrain: Magnify, O my soul, the most pure Virgin Theotokos, who is more honorable than the armies of heaven!
troparia.text:
Theotokion: The expanse of thy mighty deeds doth confine me, O Sovereign Lady,
giving me discourse, and most glorious one I am at a loss because of thy magnificence.
Wherefore, we glorify Him Who hath thus magnified thee.

troparia.refrain: Magnify, O my soul, the three pastors of the most holy Trinity!
troparia.text:
A threefold virtue hath been exalted and filled all things with glory,
shining forth upon us another thrice-radiant ray as its own effulgence:
the initiates of the mysteries of heaven, by whom we are guided in piety to divine vision.

troparia.refrain: Magnify, O my soul, the three great luminaries of the triple Sun!
troparia.text:
There is no repetition in these three, for each of them beareth the seniority:
none is first, but there is a surpassing equality of honor;
and they all-joyously credit the victory to each other,
for the audacity of jealousy, which corrupteth oneness of mind, hath no place in them.

troparia.refrain: Magnify, O my soul, the might of the indivisible Godhead in three Hypostases!
troparia.text:
The piety of the fathers, having shown forth its own firstborn sons,
through them hath begotten faithful and blameless children of the light,
who made perfect by the Spirit, Who spake through them;
asketh them to preserve, inviolate to the end, the peace which they inherited from them.

troparia.refrain: Magnify, O my soul, the most pure Virgin Theotokos, who is more honorable than the armies of heaven!
troparia.text:
Theotokion: Through the revelation of the Father,
the foremost of wise hierarchs proclaimed thy Son to be the Son of the living God, O Mother of God,
receiving knowledge of the mystery not from flesh and blood;
wherefore, glorifying thee, the Virgin, he magnified thee as Mother and Theotokos.

exapostilaria.text:
Let us praise the God-bearing fathers, the three radiant lamps
shining more brightly than the rays of the sun
with the light of the Trinity, the Author of light,
the three-Sunned Unity which is supra-naturally united.
exapostilaria.label: Exaposteilarion

exapostilaria.text:
Now let us all praise the receptacles of light, the lightning-flashes of beams of light:
Basil the Great, Gregory the Theologian and John Chrysostom.
exapostilaria.label: Another Exaposteilarion (at Glory)

exapostilaria.text:
O sole Godhead—Father, Son and Spirit—
through the entreaties of Basil, Gregory and John,
and of the most pure Theotokos,
may I not be cut off from Thy glory!
exapostilaria.label: Theotokion (at Both now)

stichera.verse: To do among them the judgment that is written: this glory shall be to all His saints. (Ps. 149:9)
stichera.text:
Rejoice, O trinity of hierarchs, great bulwark of the Church,
pillars of piety, confirmation of the faithful,
downfall of heretics,
ye who shepherded the people of Christ with divine teachings
and nurtured them with divers virtues,
O manifest preachers of grace,
who set forth laws for the fullness of Christ's Church!
O ye guides to the highest, ye gates of paradise,//
entreat Christ, that He send down great mercy upon our souls!
stichera.author: Nilus Xanthopoulus

stichera.verse: Praise God in His saints; praise Him in the firmament of His power. (Ps. 150:1)
Praise Him for His mighty deeds; praise Him according to His exceeding greatness. (Ps. 150:2)
stichera.text:
Rejoice, O trinity of hierarchs, earthly angels whose path is in the heavens,
salvation of the world, joy of mankind,
teachers of the world, champions of the Word,
most wise healers of infirmities of soul and body,
ever-flowing spiritual rivers watering the whole face of the earth with your teachings,
stairways of theology!
O ye godly ones of golden discourse,//
entreat Christ, that He send down great mercy upon our souls!
stichera.author: Nilus Xanthopoulus

stichera.verse: Praise Him with the sound of the trumpet; praise Him with the psaltery and harp. (Ps. 150:3)
stichera.text:
Rejoice, O trinity of hierarchs, ye earthly firmaments of the Sun,
rays and beacons of the effulgence of the threefold Sun,
enlightenment of the darkened,
fragrant and most beautiful flowers of paradise,
O Theologian, wise Basil and Chrysostom,
ye tablets of the Spirit inscribed by the finger of God,
ye breasts exuding the milk of salvation!
O ye adornment of wisdom,//
entreat Christ, that He grant unto our souls great mercy!
stichera.author: Nilus Xanthopoulus

theotokion.text:
Let us sound the trumpet of hymns,
for the Virgin Mother, the Queen of all,
bowing down from on high, with blessings crowneth those who hymn her.
Let kings and princes come together,
and let them clap their hands in hymns
for the Queen who gave birth to the King
Whose good pleasure it was, in His love for mankind, to loose those held by death from of old.
Ye pastors and teachers, assembling, let us praise the most pure Mother of the good Shepherd,
the lampstand of golden luster, the light-bearing cloud,
her who is more spacious than the heavens, the animate ark,
the fiery throne of the Master,
the golden jar which held the Manna, the gate of the Word which was closed,
the refuge of all Christians;
and, praising her with divinely eloquent hymns, let us say thus:
O palace of the Word, vouchsafe the kingdom of heaven unto us, the lowly;//
for nothing is impossible to thy mediation!
theotokion.author: by Germanus
theotokion.label: Theotokion at Both now

troparionAfterDoxology.text:
In that ye share in the ways of the apostles,
O teachers of the whole world,
entreat the Master of all,
that He grant peace to the world//
and great mercy to our souls.
